Per-command estimated tokens (characters/4) of raw vs rtk-filtered output across 84 bench cases (many conditional on installed tools) run on the rtk repo; a case is GOOD at >=60% savings, and the run fails on any negative or empty filter

summary: RTK publishes no measured results. Its headline figures, 'up to 90% of the bash output' and '<10ms overhead', are stated without data, and docs/contributing/TECHNICAL.md:377-379 lists <10ms as a target. scripts/benchmark.sh defines 84 bench cases that compare raw and filtered output, runs live in CI and fails on negative or empty filters, but its output is not committed and its inputs are the state of the machine and repository it runs on. docs/guide/resources/savings-explained.md states that token counts are estimates (bytes / 4) and that a command showing 90% fewer output bytes does not make a session 90% cheaper; scripts/benchmark-sessions/lib/runner.py imports modules (.config, .manifest, .session, .terminal_bench, .vm) that are not in the repository, so it cannot run.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
